scenes.headline: select()
scenes.subtitle: Choosing and shaping the columns you keep.
scenes.narration: The select transformation lets you pick which columns to keep and derive new ones from a DataFrame.

scenes.headline: What select does
items: Returns a new DataFrame with only chosen columns
Can rename with alias or compute expressions
Is a lazy transformation — nothing runs yet
scenes.narration: Select returns a new DataFrame containing only the columns you choose. It can rename columns with alias or compute expressions, it reduces data width for better performance, and it is a lazy transformation.

scenes.headline: Selecting and computing columns
scenes.code:
from pyspark.sql.functions import col

df.select(
    col("customer_id"),
    col("name"),
    (col("price") * col("qty")).alias("total")
).show()
scenes.narration: We select the customer id and name columns directly, then compute a new total column by multiplying price and quantity and naming it with alias. The result is a narrower DataFrame focused on exactly the fields we need.

scenes.text: Select early to drop unused columns — Spark reads less and runs faster.
scenes.narration: Selecting early to drop unused columns lets Spark read and shuffle less data, which speeds up the whole job.
